Definition: from G5575; to be an untrue testifier, i.e. offer falsehood in evidence:--be a false witness.
BiblicalUsage: Pseudomartyreo means to bear false witness, to offer falsehood in evidence. Jesus lists it among the commandments: Thou shalt not bear false witness. At His own trial, many bare false witness against Him, but their witness agreed not together.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the commandment was broken against the Lawgiver Himself: the men who bore false witness against Jesus broke the very law He wrote. I hold that false witness always fails in the end, because lies cannot agree with each other, only the truth agrees with itself.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
